body.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\). It then tests every structural chart for emptiness. If the margin test fails or every chart is empty, \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\), and the input is reported as incompatible and is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\). Otherwise one sampled point \(x_0\) is used in the unequal-target feasibility test on every chart, and \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\) if and only if every such refinement is empty. For design B, all structural charts are first tested for emptiness; if all are empty, \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\) and the input is reported as incompatible and non-rigid, while on a nonempty union \(\lvert\mathcal T_B(p)\rvert=1\) if and only if every chartwise unequal-target refinement from the common sample \(x_0\) is empty. These are finite observable rank, support, incidence, residual-forest, cycle, and target-agreement tests.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data. For rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval. Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\). If both selected cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness on a boundary face. Connected-component descriptions are optional diagnostics and are not part of the rigidity decision.
body.justification: The theorem is the necessary-and-sufficient causal classifier, with strict design-A margin validation before any compatibility declaration or lift.
body.gap: Regular inversion does not decide global constancy across disconnected charts and support faces or distinguish an invalid supplied margin from a feasible normalized cycle factorization.
body.consumer: Analysts receive one exact target, legal target-changing SCM twins, or a separate incompatibility report.
body.proof_tex:
By the design-A nonemptiness criterion,
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing . \tag{15}
\]
Thus the strict-interior margin test is necessary even if the normalized cycle
fiber is nonempty.  For design B, surjectivity in the cycle-to-SCM lift gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing . \tag{16}
\]
An empty fiber has an empty target image and hence cardinality zero, rather
than one.  Therefore failure of either applicable test is correctly reported
as incompatibility and is non-rigid according to PN/PS rigidity.

Suppose next that the relevant full fiber is nonempty.  The same lift lemma is
onto and preserves the causal target, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{17}
\]
The mixed-support elimination theorem writes either cycle fiber in (17) as a
finite union \(X=\bigcup_{\chi}X_{\chi}\) of its structural charts.  Its
one-sample/all-chart conclusion supplies \(x_0\in X\), puts
\(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and proves
\[
 \tau_C(X)=\{t_0\}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 X_{\chi}\cap
 \left\{x:\|\tau_C(x)-t_0\|_2^2>0\right\}=\varnothing
 \quad\text{for every }\chi . \tag{18}
\]
This is a comparison with the same \(t_0\) on every chart, so (18) also
compares disconnected components and distinct support faces.  Combining
(17)--(18) proves the asserted necessary-and-sufficient rigidity tests.

The mixed-support theorem also establishes the stated output discipline over
\(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): a field expression is returned only when constructed;
otherwise the selected coordinate is represented by a square-free
real-univariate polynomial, rational coordinate functions, and Thom signs.
For rational input, clearing guarded denominators and isolating the selected
real root gives the stated integer-polynomial and rational-isolating-interval
form.

If a refinement in (18) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies
\(\tau_C(x_1)\ne\tau_C(x_0)\).  Both points are in the same observable cycle
fiber.  Applying the cycle-to-SCM lift separately gives two legal full SCMs
with the same selected law and, in design A, the same supplied margin vector,
while target preservation gives unequal values of \(\tau\).  If both sampled
points belong to interior support charts, the interior positive-lift lemma
makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability,
and selection probability strictly interior.  That lemma has no such
conclusion when either point is on a support face, which proves exactly the
boundary qualification in the statement.  No connected-component
description was used in any implication.
